description: Use case: the sun intensity, the household electricity price and the feed-in remuneration in Switzerland for the photovoltaic return formulas of pv_yield.json, which also holds the general phrases and the self-consumption share. For twelve sample places, selected by their postal code, PVGIS 5.3 gives the yearly global horizontal irradiation, the yearly irradiation on a panel at the optimal slope and the yearly yield of one kWp; the coordinates are the centre of the town of the postal code. The household electricity price is the price of the local grid operator (ElCom 2026, consumption profile H4) and the feed-in remuneration is the federal minimum of 2026, so all three return formulas apply, e.g. 10 kWp in CH-8001 give 1152.22 kWh per kWp times 10 kWp = 11522 kWh and between 691 CHF (feed-in) and 2853 CHF (self-consumption) per year, about 1340 CHF with the self-consumption share of a terraced house; a roof that is flatter, steeper or not facing south gets less than the yield at the optimal slope.

sources.name: PVGIS 5.3
sources.description: Photovoltaic Geographical Information System version 5.3 of the European Commission Joint Research Centre, tool PVcalc queried on 8 October 2026 with the default settings: radiation database PVGIS-SARAH3 with the years 2005 to 2023, meteorological data ERA5, horizon shading calculated from the elevation model, crystalline silicon panels with a peak power of 1 kWp and 14 percent system loss, free-standing at the optimal slope and azimuth for the yield and at slope 0 for the global horizontal irradiation.

sources.name: ElCom electricity prices 2026
sources.description: Swiss Federal Electricity Commission ElCom, electricity prices of the basic supply 2026 per municipality, queried on 8 October 2026 for the consumption profile H4 and the standard product of the grid operator: the total price in Rp per kWh as published by ElCom; stored in CHF per kWh, i.e. divided by 100. For the municipality of Lucerne, where two grid operators supply, the value of ewl, which supplies the city centre of CH-6003, is used.

sources.name: Energieverordnung minimum feed-in remuneration 2026
sources.description: Swiss Energy Ordinance (EnV, SR 730.01) Art. 12 para. 1bis, in force since 1 January 2026: the grid operator pays at least 6 Rp per kWh for the electricity of photovoltaic installations of less than 30 kW; above the minimum the remuneration follows the quarterly reference market price of the Swiss Federal Office of Energy; the guarantee of origin may be paid in addition. The 6 Rp are also stated in the 2026 tariff sheets of EKZ and Repower.
